In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lectin-induced intestinal and pancreatic growth is a result of a CCK mediated mechanism.
the growth of the pancrea is stimulated via CCK release and the intestinal mucosa by a CCK-independent mechanism.
the lectin PHA stimulates CCK release in vitro and in vivo, which induces pancreatic growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PHA is a CCK releasing stimulus in vivo and in vitro and that this effect is the major cause of pancreatic growth.
the growth effect of PHA is mediated by CCK in the pancreas and by an as yet unknown mechanism in the small intestine.
